# Indiana Packers marks opening of Delphi distribution center

 Tuesday, August 18, 2026 05:42 PM EDT By Alex Brown 

(Photo courtesy of Indiana Packers Corp.)

Delphi-based Indiana Packers Corp. has cut the ribbon on its new distribution center that it says more than doubles its warehouse capacity.

The new facility will bring 30 new jobs to the company’s Carroll County operation, which already employs more than 2,000 people.

“This new facility reinforces our long-term commitment to our team members, producers, customers, Carroll County, Delphi, and the northcentral Indiana community,” Indiana Packers President and Chief Operating Officer Eric Sheiss said in written remarks.

The facility, which some reports say is the result of a $44 million investment, adds more than 96,000 square feet of new freezer space for the company and increases its frozen pallet storage capacity by more than 12 times.

The company said the facility will allow it to provide faster and more efficient shipping to customers across the United States and in more than 20 other countries.

# Averitt expands logistics network with Jackson, Mississippi, facility

 August 27, 2026 

Less-than-truckload carrier Averitt said Thursday it has opened a 100,000-square-foot distribution and fulfillment facility in Jackson, Mississippi. The announcement follows other recent investments the carrier has made to its network.

The new warehouse is near central Mississippi’s major freight lanes of I-20 and I-55. The Mississippi Department of Transportation announced Tuesday a $400 million project to improve the roadways and bridges along these corridors. The plan also calls for rail upgrades.

Most national LTL carriers have nearby service centers and Averitt operates a 57-door LTL terminal next to the new facility. 

Cookeville, Tennessee-based Averitt’s latest addition will serve rail connections and provide service to ports in New Orleans and Mobile, Alabama. Customers will be able to flex the amount of space needed for seasonal and overflow inventory projects without committing to long-term contracts.

by Shari Barbanel | September 8, 2026

Boiron USA (Newtown Square, PA) announced the grand opening and ribbon cutting for its new 78,898-square-foot logistics center will be held on Sept. 16.

Operational since a soft launch in late May 2026, the facility expands the company’s storage and distribution to support continued growth and increasing demand for its homeopathic medicine.

The new facility is located at 4400 Alice Grim Blvd. in Newtown Square about one mile from Boiron’s American headquarters. The state-of-the-art, temperature-controlled facility consolidates operations previously housed in two nearby warehouses.

It features energy-efficient mechanical systems, 24-hour surveillance, large windows for natural light, and four electric vehicle charging stations. A team of 28 employees operates the center.

# Five Star opens expanded Nashville distribution center

Image courtesy Five Star Breaktime Solutions

August 10, 2026

Five Star Breaktime Solutions has opened a consolidated regional office and distribution center in Antioch, a Nashville, Tennessee, neighborhood, according to a press release. The workplace refreshments provider said the move follows another facility relocation and upgrade completed earlier this year in Dothan, Alabama.

The 80,000-square-foot Nashville facility combines operations previously spread among four buildings totaling about 55,000 square feet. Five Star said it needed additional capacity after years of service expansion, regional economic development and customer growth across Middle Tennessee.

The new center more than doubles the size of the branch's product-picking lines and provides four times as much cold-storage capacity. It also includes a climate-controlled warehouse, a 40-person training room, an upgraded employee break room and office spaces designed to encourage collaboration.
